specialty.heading: Soakage Pits and Sub Soil Drainage
paragraphs: Need effective surface water management for your property?
We specialise in soakage pits and sub-soil drainage solutions to prevent flooding, control groundwater, and protect your foundations.
Whether you're dealing with excess water pooling or poor drainage, we ensure a durable and effective system tailored to your needs.

faqs.q: How big does a soak pit need to be?
faqs.a: A soak pit is sized to the area it drains, typically your roof and paved surfaces, and how fast your soil absorbs water. As a rule of thumb, every 10 m² of roof needs around 1 m³ of soakage in free-draining soil, but clay sites need much more. We size every pit to your site and council requirements.

faqs.q: Do soak pits work in clay soil?
faqs.a: They can, but clay absorbs water very slowly, so a standard pit often isn't enough. In Upper Hutt's clay areas we combine larger soakage areas with subsoil drainage, or connect overflow to the stormwater system. A percolation test shows what your site needs before you spend money.

faqs.q: Does a soak pit need council consent in NZ?
faqs.a: Usually yes. A soak pit is a drainage asset and new drainage work generally requires a building consent, with the design checked against your council's requirements. As certifying drainlayers we prepare the consent application and arrange inspections so your pit is legal and signed off.

faqs.q: How long does a soak pit last?
faqs.a: A properly sized and built soak pit should last 25 years or more. The usual cause of failure is sediment or fine clay clogging the soakage surface over time. Keeping sumps cleaned and the pit wrapped in the right geotextile fabric extends its life significantly.

faqs.q: How much does a soak pit cost in Upper Hutt?
faqs.a: Cost depends on pit size, depth, access for excavation and what your soil is like. Most residential soak pits are straightforward excavator jobs, and we quote fixed prices after a site visit. Get in touch for a free quote.

description: Soak pit installation and renewal in Upper Hutt, sized to your soil and consented with council. Fixed prices from certifying drainlayers.

specialty.heading: Stormwater or Sewer Drainage
paragraphs: Ensure your section is free draining with our expert stormwater drainage services.
We install, repair, and maintain drainage systems, including channel drains and sumps, to prevent surface water buildup and manage stormwater effectively.
We also handle domestic sewerage, from repair and maintenance of exisiting systems, through to installing new pre-slab drains and pipework.

faqs.q: What's the difference between stormwater and sewer drains?
faqs.a: Stormwater drains carry rainwater from roofs, driveways and yards to the stormwater system; sewer drains carry wastewater from your toilets, sinks and laundry to treatment. They're separate systems, and connecting the two is illegal, it overloads treatment plants and causes pollution.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for stormwater drains on my property?
faqs.a: You are, up to where your drain connects to the council system (usually at the boundary). From that point the council owns and maintains it. We can CCTV your drains to pinpoint exactly where your responsibility ends.

faqs.q: Do I need consent to add new stormwater drains?
faqs.a: Yes, new or altered drainage work needs a building consent in almost every case. As certifying drainlayers we handle the consent application, build to code, and arrange council inspections for sign-off.

description: Stormwater and sewer drainage in Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, new drains, channel drains, sumps and sewer pump chambers, plus repairs.

specialty.heading: Lifestyle Block Solutions, Property Water Supplies and Drainage
paragraphs: Need your lifestyle block field drains cleared out or a piped culvert drain crossing installed? Struggling to hold on to that precious rainwater? Or is your main water supply pipework leaking?

We install and repair property water supplies and drainage, fixing or renewing pipework, tanks or pumps. Providing tailored solutions for rural and urban properties, be it the water piped in from the councils toby at the street or your rural rain water tanks and overflow.

faqs.q: What are my lifestyle block water supply options?
faqs.a: Most lifestyle blocks use rainwater tanks, sometimes topped up by a bore or carted water, with a pump and pressure system to deliver house pressure. We install and repair the full setup, tanks, pumps, pipework, filters and overflow, and can fix leaking supply lines from the street toby.

faqs.q: Can you install rainwater tanks in Upper Hutt?
faqs.a: Yes, tank supply, pump and pressure vessel installation, and connecting overflow to a soak pit or drain are all regular work for us. Tanks over certain sizes may need council checking; we advise on that during the site visit.

faqs.q: My water pump keeps cycling, what's wrong?
faqs.a: Usually a failed pressure vessel, a leak downstream, or a worn pressure switch. Constant cycling wears the pump out fast. It's a quick diagnosis job, we test the vessel and switch and find any hidden leaks.

description: Lifestyle block water supplies and drainage in Upper Hutt, rain tanks, pumps, field drains, culverts and supply line repairs, supplied and installed.

specialty.heading: Hot Water Systems & Gas Leak Repairs
paragraphs: Reliable hot water solutions and leak repairs. We install and service hot water systems to keep your home running efficiently.
If you suspect a gas leak, we provide prompt and professional tests, checks and repairs to ensure safety and prevent damage.
Get in touch to talk about your specific situation.
specialty.imageAlt: Hot Water Systems and Gas Leak Testing

faqs.q: No hot water, what should I check first?
faqs.a: Check the power or gas supply is on, and look for a tripped switch or blown fuse at the hot water cylinder. If you have a gas continuous-flow unit, check the batteries in the remote or ignition. If supplies are fine and the water still runs cold, call us, the element, valve or unit itself is likely at fault.

faqs.q: Mains pressure or low pressure cylinder, which is better?
faqs.a: Mains pressure cylinders give stronger showers and let you use modern tapware; low pressure systems are cheaper in some setups but suffer weak flow. Most replacements today go to mains pressure. We assess your existing pipework and advise which suits your house and budget.

faqs.q: How long does a hot water cylinder last in NZ?
faqs.a: Typically 20–25 years for a mains pressure cylinder, less in hard-water areas. If yours is over 15 years, leaking from the seam, or running out of hot water faster than it used to, replacement is usually more economical than repair.

faqs.q: How much does hot water cylinder replacement cost?
faqs.a: It depends on cylinder size, type (mains or low pressure, electric or gas), and whether pipework needs changing over. We supply and install, and quote fixed prices after a quick site assessment.

description: Hot water cylinders in Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, mains and low pressure cylinders and Rinnai Infinity units, supplied, installed and repaired.

faqs.q: What does a drainlayer do?
faqs.a: A drainlayer installs and maintains the drains that carry stormwater, sewerage and wastewater away from your property, everything from new sewer and stormwater lines to soak pits, subsoil drainage and drain repairs. In New Zealand drainlaying is a licensed trade, so this work must be done by a certified drainlayer.

faqs.q: Do I need a certified drainlayer for drainage work?
faqs.a: Yes. Drainlaying is restricted work under the Plumbers, Gasfitters and Drainlayers Act 2006. Any new or altered sewer, stormwater or drainage work needs a certified drainlayer and, in most cases, a building consent. Pioneer PGD holds certifying drainlayer licences and we handle the consent paperwork for you.

faqs.q: Do you handle council consent for drainage work?
faqs.a: Yes. Most new drainage work, new sewer lines, stormwater systems, soak pits, needs a building consent from your local council. We prepare the application, deal with council on your behalf, and arrange inspections at the right stages so the job is signed off properly.

description: Certifying drainlayers in Upper Hutt, soak pits, sewer and stormwater drains, subsoil drainage, CCTV inspections and repairs across the Hutt Valley.

name: Blocked Drains
intro: Blocked drain clearing across Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, water jetting, root cutting and CCTV to clear the blockage and find what caused it, so it stays clear.
bullets: CCTV inspection to find the cause

faqs.q: How do I know if my drain is blocked?
faqs.a: The signs are hard to miss: sinks or the shower drain slowly, the toilet gurgles or fills higher than normal, and you may smell sewage outside. If more than one fixture backs up at once, the blockage is usually in the main drain, that's when to call us.

faqs.q: How do you clear a blocked drain?
faqs.a: We start by clearing with water jetting or drain rods, then use a CCTV camera inspection to find what caused the blockage, often tree roots, collapsed pipe or fat buildup. Clearing the symptom is quick; finding the cause stops it coming back.

faqs.q: Whose responsibility is a blocked drain?
faqs.a: Drains on your property up to the point of connection to the council main are the homeowner's responsibility. Blockages or faults beyond that point belong to the council. A CCTV inspection shows exactly where the issue sits before you pay for repairs.

description: Blocked drain clearing in Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, water jetting, root cutting and CCTV to clear the blockage and stop it coming back.

name: CCTV Drain Inspection
intro: CCTV drain camera inspections in Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, see inside your drains, find the exact fault and its depth, and get a clear report before any digging starts.

faqs.q: What does a CCTV drain inspection cost?
faqs.a: A CCTV drain inspection is an hourly-rate job and most residential inspections take under two hours, including a written report of what we find. Exact pricing depends on access and drain length, contact us for a quote.

faqs.q: What can a CCTV drain inspection find?
faqs.a: The camera shows the inside of the pipe in detail: tree root intrusion, cracks and collapsed sections, offset joints, fat buildup, and where a blockage or leak sits, with measured depths so any dig-up is precise.

faqs.q: Should I get drains checked before buying a house?
faqs.a: Yes, it's cheap insurance. Older Wellington suburbs have clay and earthenware drains that crack and invite tree roots. A pre-purchase drain inspection can reveal five-figure repair issues the building inspection won't see.

description: CCTV drain inspections in Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, see inside your drains, find the exact fault and get a clear report before digging starts.

name: Drain Repairs
intro: Drain repair and replacement in Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, CCTV-located, fixed-quote repairs using relining or renewal, with our own diggers and proper ground reinstatement.

faqs.q: How do I know if my drain needs repair?
faqs.a: Repeated blockages, slow drains across multiple fixtures, wet patches or subsidence in the yard, and rat or drain-fly problems all point to a broken drain. A CCTV inspection confirms it and shows exactly where and what the fault is.

faqs.q: How are drains repaired, do you have to dig up my yard?
faqs.a: Not always. Where the pipe has good alignment we can reline some drains with minimal digging. Where pipes have collapsed, excavation and replacement is needed, we have our own diggers and reinstate the ground properly.

faqs.q: How much does drain repair cost?
faqs.a: It depends on depth, length, access and whether relining or replacement is right. We CCTV first, then give a fixed quote, so you know the price before work starts.

description: Drain repairs in Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, CCTV-located, fixed-quote repairs using relining or renewal, with proper ground reinstatement.

faqs.a: Yes, sewer and stormwater drainage for new homes and extensions, from pre-slab pipework through to final connections and as-built sign-off. We work with your builder and arrange council inspections at each stage.

faqs.q: When should the drainlayer be involved in a new build?
faqs.a: Early. Earthworks and pre-slab drainage happen before the concrete goes down, so we plan in with your builder at slab stage and return for the sewer, stormwater and downpipe connections later.

faqs.q: Do you handle as-builts and council sign-off?

faqs.q: Are you licensed gasfitters?
faqs.a: Yes. Gasfitting is restricted work in New Zealand and must be done by a licensed gasfitter. Pioneer PGD holds a certifying gasfitting licence, the highest level, so we can install, test and certify gas appliances and pipework, and issue gas certificates of compliance.

faqs.q: Can you convert my appliance to LPG or natural gas?
faqs.a: Yes, we install and convert gas appliances for both natural gas and LPG, including Rinnai Infinity units, hobs and heaters. We also set up LPG bottle stations and property gas supplies.

faqs.q: Do you install Rinnai Infinity units?
faqs.a: Yes, new external Rinnai Infinity (continuous flow) water heaters, supplied and installed, are one of our most common gasfitting jobs. We size the unit to your household, run the new gas pipework if needed, and certify the installation.

name: Gas Leak Detection
intro: Gas leak detection and repair in Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, pressure testing, electronic detection and certified repairs for natural gas and LPG systems.
bullets: Gas leak detection and pressure testing

faqs.q: What are the signs of a gas leak in the home?
faqs.a: A rotten-egg smell (added odourant), hissing near appliances or pipework, dead or dying plants along a pipe run, and unexplained headaches or dizziness. If you smell gas strongly: turn the gas off at the bottle or meter, don't operate switches, ventilate, and call us from outside.

faqs.q: Who do I call for a gas leak in NZ?
faqs.a: For a strong smell or suspected major leak, turn off the gas at the meter or bottle and call your gas network provider, or 111 if it's dangerous. For leaks at appliances, BBQ lines or pipework on your property, call a licensed gasfitter: we detect and repair leaks and certify the fix.

faqs.q: How is a gas leak detected?
faqs.a: We pressure-test the pipework, then trace with a gas detector and leak-check every joint and appliance connection with detection fluid. Once found, we repair the leak and re-test to certify the system is gas-tight.

description: Gas leak detection and repair in Upper Hutt and the Hutt Valley, pressure testing, electronic detection and certified repairs for gas and LPG.
